problem: The conclusion is wrong for an AC-rated capacitor. An AC voltage rating is an RMS rating, so a 250 V AC capacitor is fine on a 230 V RMS supply; the peak of 325 V is already covered by the rating (its own peak rating would be about 354 V). Only a DC-rated capacitor would be stressed by the 325 V peak.
fix: A 230 V RMS sine has peak 230 × 1.414 = 325 V. A capacitor rated 250 V DC therefore cannot be used on this supply, because the peak exceeds its DC rating. An AC rating is an RMS rating, so a 250 V AC part is safe at 230 V RMS.

problem: "High crest factor warns of pulses that heat equipment more than a sine of the same RMS" reads as if heating depends on the shape. In a plain resistor, the same RMS gives the same heating. The extra heating comes from losses that depend on peak current (winding eddy and skin effects, diodes, capacitors) in real equipment.
fix: In power quality, a high crest factor warns of pulse currents whose peaks stress components, so the equipment heats more than a resistor carrying the same RMS would.
